sections.html:
Atlanta homeowners can hire a listing agent, sell privately, or accept a cash purchase of the house in its present condition. The city has 242 officially defined neighborhoods and sits in two counties, so the right route depends on the block, the shape of the house and which tax office bills it.

  • An agent suits houses in neighborhoods where buyers expect staging and professional photos.
  • A private sale is realistic when you can price from comparable sales and handle the closing paperwork.
  • A cash sale as is helps with inherited homes, worn-out rentals, repair-heavy houses and owners facing a hard deadline.

Atlanta is the Fulton County seat and spills into DeKalb County. Before you list, find out which county holds your parcel, because that decides who assesses it, who bills it and which clerk records your deed.

Atlanta had 529,110 residents in mid-2025, up 6.1 percent from 498,805 in 2020. Owners live in fewer than half of Atlanta homes, and the typical household is two people, so rental and small-household housing makes up a large share of the stock.

Citywide middles hide a wide spread. Prices swing a great deal from one of the 242 neighborhoods to the next, so use recent sales near your address as the real guide.

Three high-rise districts line up along Peachtree: Downtown, Midtown and Buckhead. Downtown has the metro area's largest office inventory, Midtown is the second-largest business district and a hub for arts and universities, and Buckhead, eight miles north of Downtown, ranks third.

Around them lie lower-density neighborhoods where the craftsman bungalow dominates. The eastside has streetcar suburbs built from the 1890s to the 1930s, among them Victorian Inman Park. Former warehouses along the Beltline and in West Midtown now hold housing, shops and galleries. In southwest Atlanta, areas near Downtown such as the West End began as streetcar suburbs, while Collier Heights and Cascade Heights keep a postwar suburban layout.

Emory University and the CDC area joined the city through an annexation effective January 1, 2018. Buyers search by neighborhood name, so put yours in the listing headline.

sections.h2: Which county taxes your house, and how to appeal
sections.html:
It depends on which side of the county line the parcel sits. Most of the city lies in Fulton County, whose Board of Assessors mails a notice each year and gives you 45 days from its date to respond. A DeKalb-side owner should read the notice from DeKalb County and ask that county's assessors about the deadline.

  • In Fulton, the dispute can cover value only, and the deadline printed on your notice governs.
  • You can file online, by mail, or at the Board of Assessors office, 141 Pryor Street, Suite 1018.
  • The form offers a hearing, arbitration or a hearing officer, and a temporary bill may arrive in the meantime.

If you are mid-appeal when you sell, tell the closing attorney so the settlement statement can reflect any temporary tax bill.

If you have rented the house by the night, the rules affect your sale. The city council passed its short-term rental ordinance, 20-0-1656, on March 15, 2021, and the rules took effect March 1, 2022. An owner or long-term tenant may hold a license for a primary residence plus one additional dwelling unit, and the license number must appear on every advertisement.

Hosts apply through the online permitting portal, which accepts applications daily. License appeals go to the Department of City Planning, and questions can go to STR@atlantaga.gov. Enforcement dates and implementation details can change, so confirm the current status with City Planning before you describe the house as a rental. Then tell buyers plainly whether the license can transfer.

The metro economy is the eighth largest in the country, and the city claims the nation's third-largest concentration of Fortune 500 companies. Coca-Cola, Home Depot, Delta Air Lines, UPS, Chick-fil-A and Norfolk Southern all have headquarters or hubs in the region. Delta, based at Hartsfield-Jackson, is the metro area's largest employer.

Georgia Tech in Midtown, Georgia State Downtown, Emory and the Atlanta University Center keep rental and starter-home demand steady in the center of the city. About 49,000 students attend 106 Atlanta Public Schools campuses, and private options include Westminster, Lovett, Pace Academy and Paideia. School questions come up early with buyers, so be ready with the zone for your address.

Many in-town streets look different from how they did a few decades ago. After neighborhood opposition stopped two freeways planned through the east side in 1975, that area became the starting point for the gentrification that later spread. Atlanta's selection for the Olympic Games brought infrastructure work that pushed investment into other parts of the city, and construction of the Beltline has spurred new building along its path.

On blocks like these, neighbors and sale prices may have changed several times in a few years, which makes recent nearby sales the most useful pricing guide. One street can mix older bungalows with newer construction, so match your comparables by age and condition, not just by distance.

Atlanta's humid subtropical climate brings hot summers and winters that are mild but variable, with about 50 inches of precipitation a year. The city is nicknamed the City in a Forest for its dense tree cover, so inspectors look hard at roofs, gutters and drainage near the foundation.

I-20, I-75 and I-85 meet here, and the combined I-75/85 Downtown Connector carries more than 340,000 vehicles a day. The I-285 Perimeter divides Inside the Perimeter from Outside the Perimeter, and buyers often search by that label. MARTA runs buses, heavy rail and a downtown loop, which matters to buyers who plan to skip the commute by car.

Georgia's transfer tax has to be paid before an Atlanta deed can be recorded. It is $1 for the first $1,000 of price or fractional part, plus 10 cents for each additional $100 or fractional part. The seller is liable unless the contract says the buyer will pay.

Because Atlanta spans two counties, the superior court clerk who records your deed is the one for the county holding the parcel. The electronic PT-61 filing runs through the clerks' authority, and questions about exemptions go to the county clerk. Your closing attorney normally files the form for you.

faqs.q: Which county handles my Atlanta property tax appeal?
faqs.a: The county the parcel sits in. Fulton County gives 45 days from the notice date, and DeKalb County sets its own procedure for the DeKalb part of Atlanta.

faqs.q: Do I need a license to rent my Atlanta house by the night?
faqs.a: Yes. The city's ordinance requires a short-term rental license, shown on every advertisement, and applications go through the online permitting portal.

faqs.q: What is the middle value of an Atlanta owner-occupied home?
faqs.a: The 2020 to 2024 survey shows $439,600. Prices vary a great deal among the 242 neighborhoods.

faqs.q: Who owes Georgia's transfer tax in an Atlanta sale?
faqs.a: The seller by default, though a contract clause can pass the cost to the buyer.

faqs.q: Can an occupied Atlanta rental be sold?
faqs.a: Yes, with the tenant and lease in place or after the lease ends. Review the lease terms before arranging showings.
